questions.question: What defines a discrete uniform distribution on $A=\{a_1,\ldots,a_n\}$?
options: $X$ has a density on an interval

questions.question: What kind of support does a discrete uniform distribution use here?
options: A finite set of real numbers

questions.question: If $A=\{a,b,c\}$ and $X$ is uniform on $A$, what is $P(X=b)$?
Why can there be no discrete uniform distribution on all of $\mathbb N=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$?
options: probability is undefined for integer outcomes
the equal masses would have to be negative
the individual values are simply too large

questions.question: How does discrete uniform relate to naive probability?
options: Both use equal likelihood over finitely many possibilities
Both model waiting time until first success, for every possible choice of input.
Both assign probability one to every value

questions.question: What would violate discrete uniformity on a support?
options: Giving one support value a different probability from another
Assigning positive mass to every listed value equally
Using real numbers as support values

questions.question: If $X$ is uniform on $\{1,2,3,4,5\}$, what is $P(X\in\{2,5\})$?

options: A biased die has infinitely many possible values
A fair die has no sample space
A biased die does not give all six values the same probability
A biased die must be continuous

questions.question: A fair six-sided die gives each face probability $1/6$. Which general rule links support size to the common mass?
options: The largest support value determines all masses
Support size determines the common mass $1/n$
Masses are unrelated to the number of support values

options: The masses sum to $1.2$, not one
